The platform is two repositories: proprietary 'VillageOS' (server Mycelium, storage layer, seed tools) and dual-licensed 'VillageOS-API' (console, CLI, services, service contract)

CI fails any build that imports engine namespaces (vos.Core, vos.Application, vos.Infrastructure, vos.Mycelium, vos.Persistence) into the public repo; only vos.Mycelium.Testing may be compiled against

Distribution is a release archive vos.Mycelium-<version>.tar.gz built from the private repo, run with 'dotnet vos.Mycelium.dll'; it needs only the .NET runtime. No OS image, installer, partition layout or OTA client is described

On first start Mycelium generates its signing key pair, creates the admin account and a first API key, and writes bootstrap-credentials.txt; VOS_MASTER_KEY encrypts the account store and signing key at rest, otherwise they are plain text with a warning
Service handlers validate inbound JWTs with Mycelium's P-256 public key, pin ES256 as the only algorithm, and check issuer, audience and lifetime (30 s clock skew)
Every handler service exposes POST /handle, GET /health (200 {status: Healthy}) and POST /shutdown

Mycelium probes a service's port before launching, retries a failing start three times then waits a cooldown, runs each launched service under a memory ceiling, health-checks every 15 seconds, and removes an externally registered service after three consecutive failures
On restart Mycelium loads each model's newest checkpoint and replays the durable record above it; older record segments are deleted once a retained checkpoint supersedes them
Backup is manual: operators are told to back up the data directory, persistence directory, asset directory and master key; no backup tool, schedule or restore command is documented
Reference deployment is one host: Caddy reverse proxy terminates TLS and routes /api to the broker on localhost:7243; machines without a public address use a Cloudflare Tunnel
A CI test enforces that every service entry point binds loopback only

The only Dockerfiles are for example echo services; the Go one builds a static binary on distroless static-debian12 and notes that Mycelium launches handlers as local daemons, so containers need host networking
CI runs on Azure Pipelines on a self-hosted pool named 'Amsterdam' that holds macOS agents only (demand Agent.OS -equals Darwin); no ARM/Linux edge build target exists
A pipeline-node service advertises typed ports at GET /manifest; tools/pipeline-playground/declare_service.py reads it to declare the service into a seed
Services self-register with POST /api/mycelium/register {handlerId, serviceName, endpointUrl, startCommand, stopEndpoint, healthEndpoint}; there is no self-deregistration
The platform separates Facts (durable, synced before answer) from Observations (sampled telemetry, queued and batched); services write observations over HTTP via RecordObservationAsync
A case-insensitive search of the repo at the pinned SHA for mqtt, modbus, opc, lora finds no device-protocol implementation; sensor data enters only through HTTP write routes
